why: Insert an interval and test overlap: because the list is already sorted and disjoint, it splits into three runs: intervals ending before the new one, intervals that overlap it (absorb them by widening start and end), and intervals after it.
hints: The list is already sorted and disjoint. Which existing intervals can the new one possibly touch?

Closed intervals [a, b] and [s, e] overlap exactly when a <= e and s <= b. Everything with end < s comes first untouched; then every interval with start <= e overlaps and is absorbed into [min starts, max ends]; the rest follows.
Three while loops with one index: copy while intervals[i][1] < s; merge while intervals[i][0] <= e; append [s, e]; copy the rest. O(n), no sort needed.
pitfalls: Closed intervals: [1,3] and [3,5] overlap and must merge.
The new interval may go first, last, or swallow every interval.
